name: Complete Atrioventricular Septal Defect with Tetralogy of Fallot
aliases: Complete AV Septal Defect with TOF

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Heart Disease Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of a complete atrioventricular septal defect involving atrial and ventricular septa with a common atrioventricular valve
Anatomic features of Tetralogy of Fallot including ventricular septal defect, overriding aorta, right ventricular outflow tract obstruction, and right ventricular hypertrophy
Echocardiographic visualization confirming both AVSD and TOF components
Presence of central cyanosis and hypoxemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Echocardiographic confirmation of complete AV septal defect combined with anatomical features of Tetralogy of Fallot
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging studies; genetic testing may support but is not diagnostic.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Central cyanosis due to right-to-left shunting
searchTerms: blue skin from heart blood mixing
central cyanosis due to heart shunt

pathognomonic.symptomName: Heart murmur characteristic of AV septal defect and right ventricular outflow obstruction
searchTerms: murmur from valve and outflow blockage
abnormal heart sounds from AV defect

common.symptomName: Tachypnea due to congestive heart failure
searchTerms: rapid breathing due to congestive heart failure
failure to gain weight as baby

common.symptomName: Poor feeding and diaphoresis during feeding
Hepatomegaly secondary to right heart failure
searchTerms: liver swelling due to right heart problems
high red blood cell count from low oxygen
polycythemia due to chronic low oxygen
irregular heart rhythms including AV block

rare.symptomName: Stroke or embolic events due to paradoxical embolism
searchTerms: embolic events due to heart shunt

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to increased pulmonary blood flow
searchTerms: high blood pressure in lungs from excess flow
pulmonary hypertension from increased blood flow
lung vessel high pressure secondary to blood overload

laboratory: Elevated hematocrit and hemoglobin due to secondary polycythemia
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating complete AV septal defect and TOF features
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and decreased pulmonary vascular markings
Cardiac MRI for detailed anatomical assessment
other: Electrocardiogram showing right ventricular hypertrophy and possible conduction abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of right ventricular outflow tract obstruction
Presence of isolated ventricular septal defect

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
Sudden onset of arrhythmia or syncope
references: Anderson RH, et al. Paediatric Cardiology. 4th ed. Churchill Livingstone; 2010.
Moller JH, et al. The Tetralogy of Fallot: Clinical and Surgical Aspects. Circulation. 2000.
